quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in handling usually means a tire has failed. If your motorcycle feels different, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What can cause a wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When a group enters a curve, what formation should they use?
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation on straightaways, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Where should you get the main information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange for a safe ride home for your friend.
Occupy your friend with activities to distract them from drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never allow a friend to ride a motorcycle after drinking. You can help by arranging another ride home, including them in other activities, keeping them from leaving until they are sober, or asking other friends to help stop them from riding.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate or brake, as both make wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and low. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: What should your lane position help you do?

options.text: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
Travel to your destination as quickly as possible.
Linger in the blind spots of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should protect your lane from other drivers and show them what you plan to do.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is considered legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate any motor vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you start riding.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Slow down at first, then speed up and pass the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down at first, then speed up and pass the dog.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it calmly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: How can you be seen better at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at all times and position your motorcycle so other drivers can see it clearly. Keep space around you to move if danger appears. Do not rely on eye contact alone—drivers may look at you but not see you.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The driver may not see you in their blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because you have no escape route.
You should only do it during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you in their blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane. Riding next to a vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you during turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control and hold onto the handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What happens when you carry a passenger or cargo?

options.text: You accelerate faster but stop slower.
You accelerate slower and stop slower.
You accelerate slower but stop faster.
You accelerate faster and stop faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: You accelerate slower and stop slower.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle slower to speed up and slower to stop.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch the vehicles ahead—their lights can help you see the road better.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by closing the throttle gradually, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Do not use your brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing to be more visible, especially at night. Bright colors with reflective materials help other drivers see you.

questions.question: If a driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: It does not mean they will give you the right of way.
They will always give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Do not trust eye contact to protect you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but fail to notice them.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Signal your turns and use your brake light.
Watch for hazards in your path.

questions.explanation: To stay safe, be visible, signal your intentions, and watch for hazards. Do not hope other drivers see you—actively make yourself seen and be ready for anything.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume that motorcycles are as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about making sure other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles. They are hard to see. Ride safely and assume that other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
Are caused by broken ignition systems.
Happen because passengers distract the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a motorcycle you are new to. Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When a group of riders is passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, the riders should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcycle riders should pass one at a time. Each rider should finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
Guarantees that the driver will yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to ensure a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists and still do not see them.
